creator: Alexander Terp
description:
There is no way to run one tai command against a config repo other than the active one, and switching the active one with `tai config set` can leave tai unable to run at all, `config set` included.

The goal was to check one config repo's profiles on a machine where another repo is active. tai has no `--config` flag and ignores `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`DefaultPaths` in `internal/state/state.go` hardcodes `~/.config/tai`), so `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<scratch> tai config set <repo>` rewrote the real `~/.config/tai/config.yaml`. The new repo's sources pointed at paths that don't exist on that machine, and every later command failed:

```
Error: loading state: loading source "tai-cli": source path does not exist: ~/src/tai
```

Recovery meant hand-editing `config.yaml`. Today the only safe way to inspect another repo is running tai with `HOME` pointed at a scratch directory.

Two changes would cover it:

1. A global `--config <repo>` flag, or a `TAI_CONFIG` env var, for read-only commands such as `show profile` and `list`. Whether it should also cover `install` is open: manifests live under `~/.config/tai/manifests` whichever repo is active, so read-only is the safe first cut.
2. `tai config set` should not load the current config's state before switching away from it, so a broken active config can always be replaced.

Honoring `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is a separate decision. It would have made the probe above safe, but a machine that already sets it would silently move tai's config, so it needs a fallback or migration if done.

(Moved from GitHub issue #12, part 2.)
title: Let commands target another config repo, and let config set recover
